behavior_in_task_description.explanation: The instruction lists each thing the tests check. Labels must match the mockup's size, weight, letter case and letter spacing (tests accept 13-15px, weight 500-700, no uppercase transform, no letter spacing). Labels over number or score columns must be right-aligned and all other labels left-aligned (tests cover numeric, metric and Delta headers, and keep text headers left). Header rows must be evenly spaced (test: group rows as tall as the column row). It also says the grid in the mockup (Run Comparison) must match, and the tests cover that grid. The test pins the column row at exactly 40px. That number is not written down, but it is the existing height and can be measured from the mockup.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: Every expected point in the instruction is tested: label typography for column and group labels in both grids, right alignment for numeric and score headers with a left-alignment guard for text headers, and even header-row heights. Many pass-to-pass tests guard against regressions.

informative_test_structure.explanation: The specs use named describe/test blocks (e.g. 'numeric column headers line up with their right-aligned values'), comments explain the fixtures and the jsdom workarounds, and assertions carry descriptive messages. The shared header-look.ts helper is well documented and split into stylesheet and cascade sections. test.sh and verifier.py are commented clearly.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: Tests and the solution are not in the image. Bug patches are applied and deleted in the same layer. Git history is replaced with a single base commit, and file timestamps are normalized. Only the two images are copied in. test.sh resets the test files and protected harness files before applying the hidden tests. Tests check the rendered styles through a real CSS cascade, not source strings. Part of the bug is injected and not present upstream, so copying the upstream fix would not solve it fully.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task is a UI/styling fix. No structured output is expected.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: The base image is pinned (node:24.22.2-alpine3.24), the repo is checked out at a fixed commit, and npm ci installs from the lockfile. Only apk packages are unpinned, which is acceptable.

typos.explanation: No typos found in paths, commands, test IDs or file names. The test files listed in test.sh and config.json match the paths in test.patch.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile copies only bugs/ (deleted right after use) and the two PNGs. tests/ and solution/ are never copied.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: Only the repo's own dependencies are installed, via npm ci (vitest, sass, postcss and tailwind are already project deps). No test-only packages are added to the image. Bash, git and python3 are general tooling needed to apply patches.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies fix.patch, a real source-code diff across several components (header classes, alignment logic, group-header weight, row heights). It does not echo final outputs.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The agent edits existing source and creates no output files. The instruction names the input image paths.
